newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia accuses Slovenia of protectionism in oil row.
newsitem.headline: Croatia accuses Slovenia of protectionism in oil row.

text.p: Croatian oil and gas monopoly INA Industrija Nafte accused Slovenia on Wednesday of limiting its operations in the neighbouring republic through a mixture of government protectionism and low-level obstacles.

"Slovenia has an image of opening itself to the world, but concrete economic examples show that it is effectively closing itself off," Hrvoje Sarinic, president of INA's supervisory board, told a news conference.
Croatia's western neighbour, among several east European front-runners for NATO and European Union membership, will have to liberalise its stance on foreign competition, he added.
INA's Slovenian subsidiary Interina Ljubljana presented the best bid at a recent international tender for three petrol stations on major roads in Slovenia, company officials said.
But a state road construction firm, DARS, awarded all three concessions to Slovenian firm Petrol after all the bids had been publicly opened.
Sarinic, also chief of staff to Croatian President Franjo Tudjman, said he had requested official explanation for this move through the Slovenian embassy in Zagreb.

"That was a month ago now but I have received no reply so far. This is totally unacceptable," he said. "And we are not talking about competition between two companies. This is the official stance of the Republic of Slovenia..."
INA said further curbs on its activities included delays in obtaining regional and local permits to upgrade its filling stations and build new ones.
It also feared proposed legislation aimed at forcing foreign firms to build or buy huge warehouses in Slovenia and banning tanker trucks, INA's main transport vehicle, for shipments of oil products.
Although direct sales on petrol stations are a meagre 4.5 percent of the Slovenian total, its market share is boosted to 25 percent through exports to local companies Petrol and OMV Istrabenz.
